novel.justification: This inspectable condition holds when the score density is bounded below and both assignment arms satisfy a uniform interior-cone or corkscrew condition at the known boundary, including smooth or polygonal geographic and administrative partitions whose opening angles stay away from zero. It excludes cusps, vanishing wedges, and arms that pinch out. The condition defines the primitive subclass and is load-bearing for both separated boundary packings and stable local estimation.

An injective \(C^{\iota+2}\) embedding covers smooth non-self-intersecting boundaries represented by geographic-information-system or spline charts, and it defines the smooth subclass and its trimmed chart.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathcal{X}_P=[-1,1]^2\), \(\gamma_P(u)=(2u-1,0)\), \(\mathcal{A}_{0,P}=\{z\in\mathcal{X}_P:z_2<0\}\), and \(\mathcal{A}_{1,P}=\{z\in\mathcal{X}_P:z_2\geq0\}\), with the displayed convention on the interface.

definitions.name: g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}
definitions.construction: For \(x\in\mathcal{B}_P\), define the canonical exact-distance regression on \([0,\infty)\) by \[g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)=\begin{cases}N_{t,P,x}(s)/Q_{t,P,x}(s),&s>0\text{ and }Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0,\\ \mu_{t,P}(x),&s=0,\\ \mu_{t,P}(x),&s>0\text{ and }Q_{t,P,x}(s)=0.\end{cases}\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}(q,L,c_{-},r_0)=\left\{P:\text{for every }n\in\mathbb{N},\text{ all member properties enumerated below hold}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}(q,\iota,L,c_{-},r_0,\rho_0)=\left\{P:\text{for every }n\in\mathbb{N},\text{ all member properties enumerated below hold}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: K_\triangle
definitions.construction: \[K_\triangle(u)=\max\{1-|u|,0\}.\] This fixed kernel is nonnegative, symmetric, Lipschitz, supported on \([-1,1]\), and positive on \((-1,1)\).

definitions.name: \widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}
definitions.construction: Define \(\widehat{\mu}_{t,h}(x)=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf{1}\{T_i=t\}K_\triangle(D_{P,x,i}/h)Y_i}{\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf{1}\{T_i=t\}K_\triangle(D_{P,x,i}/h)}\) whenever the denominator is positive, use zero otherwise, and set \(\widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}(x)=\widehat{\mu}_{1,h}(x)-\widehat{\mu}_{0,h}(x)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak{H}_{\mathrm{ang}}
definitions.construction: Coarea angular-density confounding handle: expand each arm-specific radial conditional mean as a ratio of circle-level angular integrals; vary bounded continuous score densities through shrinking-scale angular imbalances while preserving the fixed radial mass envelope; pair those imbalances with disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines and bounded or Bernoulli outcomes; and use the induced compressed likelihoods to determine both a separated-center packing and the primitive regularity that prevents such confounding.

definitions.name: \widehat{\tau}^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}
definitions.construction:
Fix an integer \(m\geq1\), a cutoff constant \(c>0\), a bandwidth \(h>0\), and \(x\in\mathcal B_P\).  Put \(v_m(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^{m-1})^\top\), let \(e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top\), and set \(S_{P,x,i}=|D_{P,x,i}|\).  At the probability-zero value \(D_{P,x,i}=0\), assign the observation to neither arm.  Define
\[
 \widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)
 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{(2t-1)D_{P,x,i}>0\}
 K_\triangle(S_{P,x,i}/h)
 v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)^\top
\]
and
\[
 \widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)
 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{(2t-1)D_{P,x,i}>0\}
 K_\triangle(S_{P,x,i}/h)
 v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)Y_i.
\]
Let
\[
 G_m=\int_0^1uK_\triangle(u)v_m(u)v_m(u)^\top\,du,
 \qquad \lambda_m(c)=c\lambda_{\min}(G_m),
\]
and define the stabilized arm intercept and arm difference by
\[
 \widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h,c}(x)
 =\begin{cases}
 e_1^\top\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}^{-1}
 \widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h),
 &\lambda_{\min}\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}\geq\lambda_m(c)/2,\\
 0,&\lambda_{\min}\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}<\lambda_m(c)/2,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)
 =\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{1,h,c}(x)
 -\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{0,h,c}(x).
\]
The cutoff input \(c\) is suppressed from the notation for \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\).  The formula is defined for every \(h>0\); in an order-\(m\) coarea class it is used with \(c=\underline c\) and \(0<h\leq r_*\).  The strict sign convention, eigenvalue cutoff, inverse branch, and zero branch make this a pointwise Borel formula of \(U_{n,P}(x)\).

statements.justification: The bounded density supplies the upper half of local mass control, so the class needs only the primitive lower-thickness condition.
statements.gap: This is a supporting consequence of the density envelope rather than an additional Ahlfors-type premise.
statements.consumer: The local-constant stochastic bound and its population denominator use this estimate uniformly over boundary points.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}\), injectivity and \(C^1\) regularity give \[\mathcal{H}^1(\mathcal{B}_P)=\int_0^1\lVert\gamma_P'(u)\rVert_2\,du,\qquad L^{-1}\leq\mathcal{H}^1(\mathcal{B}_P)\leq L.\]
statements.justification: The smooth class obtains its curve-length control from primitive chart conditions rather than a redundant membership assumption.
statements.gap: This standard geometric identity is supporting infrastructure, not a separate statistical contribution.
statements.consumer: The uniform stochastic bound covers the trimmed curve by a number of balls controlled by the derived length envelope.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).  The smooth-embedding assumption makes \(\gamma_P\) an injective \(C^1\) map, while the speed assumption gives \(\lVert\gamma_P'(u)\rVert_2>0\) for every \(u\).  Thus the standard change-of-parameter formula for the length of a regular injective curve gives
\[
\mathcal H^1(\mathcal B_P)=\int_0^1\lVert\gamma_P'(u)\rVert_2\,du.
\]
The lower speed bound yields
\[
\mathcal H^1(\mathcal B_P)\geq\int_0^1L^{-1}\,du=L^{-1}.
\]
The chart-derivative envelope includes \(\sup_u\lVert\gamma_P'(u)\rVert_2\leq L\), and hence
\[
\mathcal H^1(\mathcal B_P)
\leq\int_0^1L\,du=L.
\]
All boundary and endpoint conditions are covered by the parameter interval \([0,1]\), so no additional endpoint term occurs.

statements.statement: For the fixed kernel \(K_\triangle\), there is \(\kappa_0=\kappa_0(c_{-},r_0)>0\) such that, for all sufficiently small \(h\), \[\inf_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}}\inf_{t\in\{0,1\}}\inf_{x\in\mathcal{B}_P}\Psi^{(0)}_{t,P,x}(h)\geq\kappa_0,\qquad \inf_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}}\inf_{t\in\{0,1\}}\inf_{x\in\mathcal{B}_{P,\delta}}\Psi^{(0)}_{t,P,x}(h)\geq\kappa_0.\]
statements.justification: This theorem-local support verifies denominator stability for the one fixed degree-zero estimator used in both distance upper bounds.
statements.gap: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance uses a broader high-level Gram condition for local-polynomial upper theory; this lemma derives only the scalar bound needed by the fixed triangular local-constant estimator.
statements.consumer: The rectifiable and smooth distance upper bounds use the same stable estimator without quantifying over kernels or polynomial degrees.
statements.proof_tex:
Take \(0<h\leq2r_0\).  The triangular kernel satisfies \(K_\triangle(u)\geq1/2\) whenever \(|u|\leq1/2\).  On \(\{T=t,\ \lVert X-x\rVert_2<h/2\}\), deterministic assignment and the definition of signed distance give \(|D_{P,x}|/h<1/2\).  Therefore, for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Psi^{(0)}_{t,P,x}(h)
&=\frac1{h^2}\mathbb E_P\!\left[K_\triangle(D_{P,x}/h)\mathbf1\{T=t\}\right]\\
&\geq\frac1{2h^2}P\{X\in\mathcal A_{t,P}\cap B_2(x,h/2)\}\\
&\geq\frac1{2h^2}c_-\left(\frac h2\right)^2
=\frac{c_-}{8}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The last inequality is the uniform two-sided-thickness assumption, whose radius condition holds because \(h/2\leq r_0\).  The same calculation applies to every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\) and every \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\subseteq\mathcal B_P\).  Thus one may take \(\kappa_0=c_-/8>0\).  This also records the required bandwidth boundary condition explicitly.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}\cup\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}\), \(x\in\mathcal{B}_P\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), coarea gives, for \(0<r\leq r_0\), \[P\{X\in\mathcal{A}_{t,P}\cap B_2(x,r)\}=\int_0^r Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds\geq c_{-}r^2.\] Hence the set \(\{s>0:Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\}\) accumulates at zero, without requiring positivity at every radius. For Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\) with \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\), \(g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)=N_{t,P,x}(s)/Q_{t,P,x}(s)\) is a version of \(\mathbb{E}_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]\). The canonical values on zero-denominator radii satisfy \[|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq Ls,\qquad s\geq0,\] and therefore \[\tau_P(x)=\lim_{s\downarrow0}\bigl(g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P,x}(s)-g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P,x}(s)\bigr).\]
statements.justification: The lemma makes exact-distance conditioning well posed without asserting that every circle has positive arm density and shows that the canonical representative identifies the boundary contrast.
statements.gap: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance, Theorem 1, supplies the identification background; this supporting lemma makes the coarea version and its behavior on zero-denominator radii explicit for the present primitive classes.
statements.consumer: The two distance-only frontier theorems use this canonical radial regression for their bias calculations and causal interpretation.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a displayed law, boundary point, and arm.  Let \(A=\mathcal A_{t,P}\cap\mathcal X_P\).  The map \(z\mapsto\lVert z-x\rVert_2\) is Lipschitz and has gradient of norm one away from \(x\), a Lebesgue-null point.  The coarea formula and the density of \(X\) therefore give, for \(r>0\),
\[
P\{X\in A\cap B_2(x,r)\}
=\int_0^r\int_{\partial B_2(x,s)\cap A}f_P(z)\,d\mathcal H^1(z)\,ds
=\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\]
For \(0<r\leq r_0\), the thickness assumption bounds this expression below by \(c_-r^2\).  In particular, every interval \((0,r)\) with \(r\leq r_0\) contains a radius at which \(Q_{t,P,x}>0\); otherwise the nonnegative integral would vanish.  Hence the positive-denominator radii accumulate at zero.  Notice that this conclusion neither states nor requires positivity at every radius.

Rectifiability of \(\mathcal B_P\) implies two-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero, and the same is true for a smooth embedded curve.  Since \(X\) has a Lebesgue density, \(P(X\in\mathcal B_P)=0\).  Deterministic assignment therefore makes the sign of \(D_{P,x}\) identify the arm almost surely.  Applying coarea once to the joint measure of \((Y,D_{P,x})\), and using consistency, shows that the radial marginal density in arm \(t\) is \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)\), while its outcome-weighted density is
\[
\int_{\partial B_2(x,s)\cap\mathcal A_{t,P}\cap\mathcal X_P}
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z,T=t]f_P(z)\,d\mathcal H^1(z)
=N_{t,P,x}(s)
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\).  Here consistency and deterministic assignment give \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z,T=t]=\mu_{t,P}(z)\) on arm \(t\).  The Radon--Nikodym characterization of conditional expectation then yields
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]
=\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every positive radius with positive denominator.

Because \(q\geq1\), membership in the stated H\"older ball gives the Lipschitz bound
\(|\mu_{t,P}(z)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq L\lVert z-x\rVert_2\).  If \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\), the ratio \(N/Q\) is a weighted average over points at distance \(s\), whence
\[
\left|\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}-\mu_{t,P}(x)\right|
\leq\frac{\int Ls f_P\,d\mathcal H^1}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}=Ls.
\]
If \(s=0\), or if \(s>0\) and \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)=0\), the canonical definition sets the regression equal to \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\), so the same inequality holds.  Consequently
\[
\lim_{s\downarrow0}g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)=\mu_{t,P}(x).
\]
Subtracting the two arm limits and using the definition of the causal target gives
\[
\lim_{s\downarrow0}\{g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P,x}(s)-g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P,x}(s)\}
=\mu_{1,P}(x)-\mu_{0,P}(x)=\tau_P(x).
\]
Thus the canonical radial regression identifies the causal contrast at the boundary; it does not redefine that contrast.

statements.statement:
There are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1/8\), depending only on the law-class parameters and \(\delta\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), one can construct \(M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}\) centers on a trimmed straight boundary, separated by a constant multiple of \(a_n^{1/q}\), and a finite hypercube family of laws in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\cap\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).  The assignment interface is straight; the regressions are disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines; every \(f_P\) is continuous and stays within the fixed density envelope; and the variance, tail, and arm-specific local-mass constants are common.  If two vertices differ only in the coordinate attached to a center \(x_j\), their target curves differ by at least \(c_1a_n\) at \(x_j\), both arm-specific radial mass densities at \(x_j\) agree at every radius, their arm-specific radial laws at \(x_j\) agree outside radii of order \(a_n\), and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathbb Q_{n,P_\omega,x_j},\mathbb Q_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}},x_j}\right)
 \leq\alpha\log M_n.
\]
The perturbations use \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\), and the density envelope and arm-specific local-mass bounds hold uniformly over the whole hypercube.  If \(L>4\), the construction may be made on the canonical square, in which case the entire family also lies in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\).
statements.proof_tex:
We prove the statement and check all support, geometric, positivity, moment, and division conditions.

First use the unit square \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\), the lower and upper half-square assignment regions, and the interface
\[
\mathcal B=\{(u-1/2,0):0\leq u\leq1\},
\qquad \gamma(u)=(u-1/2,0).
\]
The base score density is \(f_*=1\).  The chart has length one, speed one, all derivatives of order at least two equal to zero, and \(C^{\iota+2}\)-norm at most one.  The line segment is closed and convex, hence every point in the plane has a unique metric projection onto it and its reach is infinite.  Thus the speed, derivative, and reach requirements hold for every \(L\geq4\), \(\iota\geq1\), and \(\rho_0>0\).  At an endpoint, the intersection of an arm and a sufficiently small boundary ball contains a quarter disk.  Since all densities constructed below are at least \(3/4\), for \(r\leq r_0\leq1/4\) each arm has mass at least \(3\pi r^2/16\), which exceeds \(c_-r^2\) because \(c_-\leq1/(16L)\).  Compact support and the assignment-partition conditions are immediate.

Choose a nonnegative radial \(C^\infty\) function \(\phi\), supported in the open unit disk, with \(\phi(0)=1\).  Put
\[
\Delta=d a_n,
\qquad
w=(d_1\Delta)^{1/q},
\]
where the fixed constants are selected below.  Pack the interval \(\gamma([\delta,1-\delta])\) by centers \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) separated by at least \(3w\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), the disks \(B_2(x_j,w)\) are disjoint and contained in the unit square at a positive distance from the chart endpoints, and elementary interval packing gives
\[
M\geq c w^{-1}\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}.
\]
Let \(\phi_j(z)=\phi((z-x_j)/w)\).  For every derivative order \(k\leq q\),
\[
\lVert D^k(\Delta\phi_j)\rVert_\infty
\leq C_\phi\Delta w^{-k}
\leq C_\phi d_1^{-1}.
\]
Since the supports are disjoint, the same bound holds for every signed sum.  Taking \(d_1\) sufficiently large and the fixed affine slope \(b>0\) sufficiently small therefore puts all regressions below in the prescribed \(q\)-H\"older ball.

For \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^M\), define
\[
p_{0,\omega}(z)=\frac12,
\qquad
p_{1,\omega}(z)=\frac12+bz_1+\Delta\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_j\phi_j(z).
\]
After decreasing \(b\) and \(d\), these functions take values in \([1/4,3/4]\).  Conditional on \(X=z\), take independent variables
\[
Y(t)=B_t+\varepsilon_t,
\qquad
B_t\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_{t,\omega}(z)),
\qquad
\varepsilon_t\sim N(0,1).
\]
Then \(\mu_{t,P_\omega}=p_{t,\omega}\) and
\(1\leq\sigma^2_{t,P_\omega}\leq5/4\), which lies in \([L^{-1},L]\).  Hoeffding's lemma and the Gaussian moment-generating identity give
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[e^{\lambda\{Y(t)-p_{t,\omega}(X)\}}\mid X\right]
\leq e^{\lambda^2/8}e^{\lambda^2/2}
\leq e^{L^2\lambda^2/2},
\]
so the tail condition is uniform.

It remains to hide each regression bump in the radial experiment at its own center.  In polar coordinates \(z=x_j+r(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\), take a continuous cutoff \(\chi\) satisfying \(\chi(v)=0\) for \(v\leq1\) and \(\chi(v)=1\) for \(v\geq2\), and set
\[
A_n(r)=-\frac{2\Delta\phi(r/w)}{br}\,
\chi\!\left(\frac{br}{8\Delta}\right).
\]
There is no division at zero because the cutoff is identically zero on a neighborhood of zero.  On its active region \(br\geq8\Delta\), \(\lvert A_n(r)\rvert\leq1/4\), and smooth compact support of \(\phi\) makes the correction continuous at the outer edge.  Because the disks are disjoint, the formula
\[
f_\omega(z)=1+\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_jA_n(\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2)
\frac{z_1-(x_j)_1}{\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2}
\mathbf1\{z\in B_2(x_j,w)\}
\]
is unambiguous, with the summand defined as zero at \(x_j\).  Its angular correction integrates to zero on every full circle, so \(\int_Sf_\omega=1\); it is continuous and belongs to \([3/4,5/4]\subseteq[L^{-1},L]\).

Now compare adjacent vertices \(\omega\) and \(\omega^{(j)}\).  On either half-circle centered at \(x_j\), \(\int\cos\theta\,d\theta=0\).  Hence both arm-specific radial mass densities agree at \(x_j\) at every radius.  On the treated upper half-circle, whenever \(br\geq16\Delta\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\int_0^\pi p_{1,\omega}(x_j+r e_\theta)\{1+A_n(r)\cos\theta\}\,d\theta
-\int_0^\pi p_{1,\omega^{(j)}}(x_j+r e_\theta)\,d\theta\\
&\qquad=\pi\Delta\phi(r/w)+\frac\pi2brA_n(r)=0,
\end{aligned}
\]
after orienting the adjacent pair so that \(\omega_j=1\).  The control equality follows from its constant regression.  A Bernoulli variable followed by the common Gaussian channel is determined, after angular mixing at a fixed radius, by the averaged Bernoulli success probability.  Thus the entire arm-specific radial laws agree outside \(r\leq16\Delta/b\), not only their conditional means.

Inside this radius, the common radial density is bounded by \(Cr\), all Bernoulli probabilities remain in \([1/4,3/4]\), and their radially averaged success probabilities differ by at most \(C\Delta\).  The inequalities \(\log u\leq u-1\) and data processing through the common Gaussian channel give
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p,p')\leq\frac{(p-p')^2}{p'(1-p')},
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(B+\varepsilon,B'+\varepsilon)\leq\operatorname{kl}(p,p').
\]
Consequently one compressed observation satisfies
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P^{\mathrm{dist}}_{\omega,x_j},P^{\mathrm{dist}}_{\omega^{(j)},x_j})
\leq C\int_0^{16\Delta/b}\Delta^2r\,dr
\leq C'\Delta^4.
\]
Tensorization gives \(C'n\Delta^4=C'd^4\log n\).  Moreover
\[
\log M=\left(\frac{1}{4q}+o(1)\right)\log n.
\]
Choosing \(d\) sufficiently small gives the asserted bound for a fixed \(\alpha<1/8\), with enough slack that Poissonization at mean \(2n\) still has exponent below one.  At \(x_j\), the adjacent target curves differ by \(\Delta\phi_j(x_j)=d a_n\), so \(c_1=d\).  The global density bounds already proved, together with the fixed half-square geometry, give common upper and lower arm-mass envelopes over the entire hypercube.  This completes membership in both \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).

For the canonical square \([-1,1]^2\), use the required chart \(\gamma(u)=(2u-1,0)\) and base density \(f_*=1/4\).  When \(L>4\), let \(\varepsilon_L=1-4/L>0\), replace the cutoff constant \(8\) by a constant \(C_L\geq4/\varepsilon_L\), and choose \(d_1\) sufficiently large and then \(d/b\) sufficiently small as functions of \(L\).  The first choice keeps the cancellation region inside every bump also when \(q=1\); the second keeps its radius and all bump disks away from the trimmed endpoints for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The relative density perturbation is then at most \(\varepsilon_L/2\), so
\[
L^{-1}\leq\frac14(1-\varepsilon_L/2)\leq f_\omega
\leq\frac14(1+\varepsilon_L/2)\leq L.
\]
The cancellation and divergence calculations are unchanged up to constants depending on \(L\).  This verifies the canonical-square clause for \(L>4\).  At \(L=4\), the lower envelope \(f\geq1/4\) on a square of area four and normalization force \(f\equiv1/4\), so no nonzero angular density perturbation is possible; no canonical-square claim is made in that boundary case.
statements.justification: This explicit compressed-experiment construction converts angular-density confounding into the logarithmic uniform lower bound even under a perfectly smooth interface and smooth outcome regressions.
statements.gap: The published pointwise converse does not distribute continuous angular-density perturbations over separated trimmed-boundary centers with a logarithmic divergence budget.
statements.consumer: The rectifiable, smooth, and strict-slack straight-class distance converses use this family together with the coordinatewise overlap argument.

statements.statement: For every \(q\geq1\), there exist constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{rect}}\leq C_{\mathrm{rect}}<\infty\), depending only on \(q,L,c_{-},r_0\), such that \[c_{\mathrm{rect}}\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}})}{a_n}\leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}})}{a_n}\leq C_{\mathrm{rect}}.\] The upper inequality is attained by the fixed degree-zero triangular-kernel estimator \(\widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}\) with \(h\asymp a_n\). The lower inequality is supplied by the separated compressed-experiment family in \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\). This theorem concerns the explicitly defined primitive two-sided-thickness class and asserts no inclusion in, or same-class tightening of, the nonparametric class in Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 6.
statements.justification: The theorem gives the sharp logarithm-bearing uniform frontier for the primitive rectifiable coordinatewise-distance experiment.
statements.gap: The published lower bound is pointwise in its packing architecture.  This theorem obtains the logarithmic factor on a separately defined two-sided-thickness class and makes no class-inclusion claim.
statements.consumer: Distance-based boundary analyses receive a rate-sharp bandwidth and worst-case uniform error guarantee under an inspectable arm-mass condition.
statements.proof_tex:
All constants below depend only on \(q,L,c_-,r_0\).  We first construct one estimator that works for every law in the class.  For an arm \(t\) and boundary point \(x\), write
\[
W_{i,t,x}(h)=\mathbf1\{T_i=t\}K_\triangle(D_{P,x,i}/h),
\qquad
G_{t,x}(h)=\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^nW_{i,t,x}(h).
\]
The local-constant estimate is the weighted outcome average when \(G_{t,x}(h)>0\), and is zero otherwise.  It is a measurable function of \(U_{n,P}(x)\), so its arm difference belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\).  By the stability lemma,
\[
\inf_{P,t,x}\mathbb E_PG_{t,x}(h)\geq\kappa_0
\]
for \(h\leq2r_0\).  By the upper-mass lemma, a kernel summand is nonzero with probability at most \(\pi Lh^2\).

We record the uniform stochastic calculation.  Conditional sub-Gaussianity, boundedness of the kernel, and the preceding support probability imply the Bernstein moment bounds
\[
\mathbb E_P|W_{i,t,x}(h)\{Y_i-\mu_{t,P}(X_i)\}|^k
\leq k!C^k h^2,
\qquad k\geq2,
\]
uniformly in \(P,t,x\); the same bounds without the outcome factor hold for centered Gram summands.  Exponential Markov optimization therefore gives, for \(0<u\leq1\),
\[
\Pr_P\!\left(\left|G_{t,x}(h)-\mathbb E_PG_{t,x}(h)\right|>u\right)
+\Pr_P\!\left(\left|\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^nW_{i,t,x}(h)
\{Y_i-\mu_{t,P}(X_i)\}\right|>u\right)
\leq C e^{-cnh^2u^2}.
\]

Choose a maximal \(n^{-3}\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B_P\).  Since \(\mathcal B_P\subseteq[-L,L]^2\), disjoint ambient disks show that this net has at most \(Cn^6\) points, independently of the curve's length.  The reverse triangle inequality and the Lipschitz property of \(K_\triangle\) show that moving the center by \(d\) changes a scaled Gram average by at most \(Cd h^{-3}\), and changes the scaled outcome average by at most
\[
Cd h^{-3}\left(\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n|Y_i|\right).
\]
The outcome envelope implies \(\sup_P\mathbb E_PY^2<\infty\).  A union bound over the net and the two arms, followed by the preceding oscillation inequalities, yields an event \(E_{n,h}\) with
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}}P(E_{n,h}^c)\leq Cn^{-12}
\]
such that, uniformly over all boundary points, every denominator is at least \(\kappa_0/2\) and every centered numerator is at most
\[
C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}.
\]
At \(h\asymp a_n\), the mesh oscillations are negligible because \(n^{-3}h^{-3}=o(a_n)\).  This argument uses an ambient-square net and hence requires no uniform boundary-length envelope or density-continuity modulus.

On the support of \(W_{i,t,x}(h)\), the H\"older assumption with \(q\geq1\) gives
\(|\mu_{t,P}(X_i)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq Lh\).  Dividing the weighted decomposition by the denominator on \(E_{n,h}\) gives
\[
\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}|\widehat\mu_{t,h}(x)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|
\leq C\left\{h+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}\right\}.
\]
On \(E_{n,h}^c\), a nonzero local-constant estimate is a convex combination of observed outcomes and hence is bounded by \(\max_i|Y_i|\); the zero-denominator branch is zero, and \(\sup_x|\tau_P(x)|\leq2L\).  Uniform sub-Gaussianity gives \(\sup_P\mathbb E_P\max_i|Y_i|^2\leq C\log n\).  Cauchy--Schwarz therefore makes the exceptional contribution \(O(n^{-6}\sqrt{\log n})\).  Taking the arm difference and then \(h\asymp a_n\) yields
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}}\mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}
|\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
\leq Ca_n,
\]
because \(h\) balances \(h\) with \(\sqrt{\log n/(nh^2)}\).  This proves the minimax upper bound with one data-driven member of the declared decision class.

For the converse, use the hypercube of \(M=M_n\) laws and centers from the angular-density packing.  Poissonize the observations with mean \(2n\) and attach independent continuous ordering marks.  Conditional on independent uniform hypercube bits, decompose the marked Poisson process into the disjoint bump cells \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) and the complement \(Z_0\).  The channels are conditionally independent, \(Z_j\) depends only on bit \(j\), and \(Z_0\) is bit-independent.  Let \(S_j\) retain from cell \(j\) only outcomes, signed radii about \(x_j\), and ordering marks.  A coordinatewise distance decoder at \(x_j\), even after being given \(Z_{-j}\) and \(Z_0\), is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\).

Poisson relative entropy equals intensity times one-observation relative entropy.  The fixed-sample packing bound and equality of adjacent radial laws outside the local cell give
\[
\operatorname{KL}\{\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=0),
\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=1)\}
\leq2\alpha\log M.
\]
Since \(2\alpha<1\), the coordinatewise-overlap direct-product lemma implies probability at least \(1/2-o(1)\) of at least one bit error.  Midpoint thresholding of the estimated target at each center converts sup-norm error below \(c_1a_n/2\) into simultaneous correct decoding.  Hence every coordinatewise distance rule in the mean-\(2n\) Poisson experiment has Bayes expected sup-norm loss at least \(ca_n\).

To return to exactly \(n\) observations, start with any fixed-\(n\) rule.  In the marked Poisson experiment, if the count is at least \(n\), apply it to the \(n\) observations with smallest marks; otherwise output zero.  Conditional on having at least \(n\) points, the selected sample is i.i.d. from \(P\), while the Poisson lower-tail Chernoff inequality gives \(\Pr\{\operatorname{Poi}(2n)<n\}\leq e^{-cn}\).  Since \(\sup_x|\tau_P(x)|\leq2L\),
\[
ca_n\leq \sup_P\mathbb E_P^{\operatorname{Poi}(2n)}[\text{sup-loss}]
\leq \sup_P\mathbb E_P^n[\text{sup-loss}]+2Le^{-cn}.
\]
Taking the infimum over fixed-sample rules proves \(R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}})\geq c'a_n\).  Combining the two inequalities gives the asserted positive finite liminf and limsup constants.  The hard family is contained directly in the project-defined class; no relation to the different class of Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 6, is used.

statements.statement: Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\). For every \(q\geq1\) and \(\iota\geq1\), there exist constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}\leq C_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}<\infty\), depending only on \(q,\iota,L,c_{-},r_0,\rho_0,\delta\), such that \[c_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}})}{a_n}\leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}})}{a_n}\leq C_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}.\] The upper inequality is attained by \(\widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}\) with \(h\asymp a_n\) and uses only the first-order continuity implied by \(q\geq1\), arm-specific local mass, and the fixed triangular kernel. The lower inequality is attained by the straight-interface, compact-support hard family in the narrowed \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\); its regressions are disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines, and its bounded continuous score densities have no common modulus.
statements.proof_tex:
All constants may depend on \(q,\iota,L,c_-,r_0,\rho_0,\delta\), but not on \(n\) or \(P\).  Apply the local-constant construction on \(\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\).  The stability lemma supplies a denominator lower bound \(\kappa_0\), the density lemma supplies probability at most \(\pi Lh^2\) for every kernel window, and \(q\geq1\) supplies the bias bound \(Lh\).  A maximal \(n^{-3}\)-separated subset of the trimmed curve has at most \(Cn^6\) points because the entire curve lies in \([-L,L]^2\).  Bernstein's inequality for the bounded kernel terms and the conditionally sub-Gaussian outcome terms, a union bound over this ambient net, and the Lipschitz oscillation of the kernel give
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}}
\mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
|\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
\leq C\left\{h+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}\right\}.
\]
For completeness, on the concentration complement a nonzero local-constant estimate is a convex combination of outcomes, while a zero denominator produces zero; uniform sub-Gaussianity and Cauchy--Schwarz make this contribution negligible.  Taking \(h\asymp a_n\) proves the upper bound.  No common modulus for \(f_P\) is used.

For the lower bound, use the unit-square version of the angular-density packing.  Its straight interface is a \(C^\infty\) injective chart, its speed and derivatives satisfy the common envelopes, its line segment has infinite reach, and all centers lie on \(\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\).  Thus every vertex is in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\) for every \(\iota\geq1\).  Poissonize at mean \(2n\), split the process into its disjoint bump cells and complement, and compress cell \(j\) to the signed-radius observations seen at \(x_j\).  The packing gives adjacent separation \(c_1a_n\) and local relative entropy at most \(2\alpha\log M_n\), with \(2\alpha<1\).  The coordinatewise-overlap direct-product lemma therefore bounds the probability of simultaneous bit recovery away from one.  Midpoint thresholding converts sup-norm loss below \(c_1a_n/2\) into simultaneous recovery.  Subsampling the first \(n\) marked observations when the Poisson count exceeds \(n\), and using its exponentially small lower tail, gives
\[
R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}})\geq ca_n.
\]
Together with the upper bound this proves the two-sided limit-rate statement.  The lower family uses disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines and bounded continuous score densities with no common modulus, exactly as asserted.
statements.justification: The theorem isolates a genuine information bottleneck: smooth assignment geometry alone cannot accelerate coordinatewise distance estimation uniformly over densities lacking a shared angular regularity modulus.
statements.gap: The published smooth-bias calculation is fixed-law and does not provide a class-uniform higher-order constant under only bounded continuity of the score density.
statements.consumer: Analysts with a smooth assignment map learn when the stable degree-zero distance procedure is the honest uniform default.

statements.statement:
Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\).  On the nonempty canonical class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\),
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
If \(L>4\), then
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp a_n,
\]
and the distance lower bound is direct from the canonical-square version of the narrowed \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\).  If \(L=4\), then the density envelope and the fixed square support force \(f_P\equiv1/4\), and
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
Consequently the distance and location exponents are strictly separated for \(q>1\) when \(L>4\), while they coincide when \(q=1\) and also throughout the no-density-slack boundary case \(L=4\).
statements.proof_tex:
All constants below may depend on the frozen class parameters, \(q\), and \(\delta\), but not on \(n\) or \(P\).

First, the class is nonempty.  Take \(X\) uniform on \([-1,1]^2\), use the prescribed half-squares and chart, take constant regressions in \((1/4,3/4)\), and let each potential outcome be a Bernoulli variable with that conditional mean plus an independent standard Gaussian.  The density is \(1/4\), the chart has speed two and zero higher derivatives, the segment has infinite reach, and each arm contains a quarter disk at a boundary endpoint.  Thus arm mass is at least \(\pi r^2/16\geq c_-r^2\).  Conditional variances lie in \([1,5/4]\), and Hoeffding's lemma times the Gaussian moment-generating function gives the required sub-Gaussian envelope.  Every support, positivity, smoothness, variance, tail, reach, chart, and boundary condition is satisfied.

For the full-location upper bound, let \(r_q(u)\) collect the bivariate monomials of total degree at most \(q-1\), let \(K_2(u)=(1-\lVert u\rVert_2)_+\), and form the usual arm-specific local-polynomial Gram matrix and outcome vector, scaled by \((nh^2)^{-1}\).  For a trimmed boundary point and sufficiently small \(h\), the rescaled arm support contains a fixed open half-disk.  The density lower envelope gives, for every coefficient vector \(v\),
\[
v^\top\mathbb E_P\widehat G_{t,x}(h)v
\geq L^{-1}\int_{H_t\cap B_2(0,1/2)}K_2(u)\{v^\top r_q(u)\}^2\,du.
\]
A nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on this open set.  Compactness of the unit sphere in the fixed-dimensional coefficient space therefore supplies a uniform positive minimum eigenvalue.  Use the intercept when the empirical minimum eigenvalue exceeds half this constant and zero otherwise.

Bounded kernel weights, the density upper envelope, and conditional sub-Gaussianity give, uniformly over a polynomial-size grid on the trimmed segment,
\[
\lVert\widehat G_{t,x}(h)-\mathbb E_P\widehat G_{t,x}(h)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\left\lVert\frac1{nh^2}\sum_iW_{i,t,x}(Y_i-\mu_{t,P}(X_i))r_q((X_i-x)/h)\right\rVert_2
\leq C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}
\]
outside an event of probability at most \(Cn^{-12}\).  Kernel Lipschitz continuity extends the bound between grid points.  Taylor's formula through total degree \(q-1\) gives bias \(Ch^q\).  The cutoff bounds the inverse on its active branch; on its failed branch the estimate is zero.  The raw outcome vector is bounded by \(Ch^{-2}n^{-1}\sum_i|Y_i|\), so Cauchy--Schwarz makes the exceptional-event expectation negligible.  Hence
\[
R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})
\leq C\left\{h^q+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}\right\}.
\]
Balancing at \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2q+2)}\) gives the upper bound \(Cs_{n,q}\).

For the full-location converse, choose \(M\asymp h^{-1}\) trimmed centers with disjoint radius-\(h\) disks.  Keep the uniform density and control regression fixed, and perturb the treated regression in alternative \(j\) by
\[
\Delta\phi((z-x_j)/h),\qquad \Delta=\eta h^q,
\]
where \(\phi\in C_c^\infty(B_2(0,1))\), \(\phi(0)=1\), and \(\eta>0\) is small.  Since \(\lVert D^k(\Delta\phi((\cdot-x_j)/h))\rVert_\infty\leq C\eta h^{q-k}\) for \(k\leq q\), every alternative lies in the same H\"older ball.  Gaussian-noised Bernoulli outcomes keep all variance and tail conditions fixed.  Relative entropy from the null obeys
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
\leq Cn\Delta^2h^2=C\eta^2nh^{2q+2}.
\]
At the chosen bandwidth this is at most a small multiple of \(\log M\).  For a uniform alternative index \(J\), the log-sum inequality gives \(I(J;O_{1:n})\leq\alpha\log M\), while conditioning entropy on the decoding-error indicator gives \(H(J\mid O_{1:n})\leq\log2+p_e\log M\).  Thus \(p_e\geq1-\alpha-o(1)\).  Sup-norm accuracy below \(\Delta/2\) decodes \(J\), proving
\[
R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\geq c h^q=cs_{n,q}.
\]

Suppose \(L>4\).  The degree-zero distance estimator has bias \(Ch\), stable denominator by two-sided thickness, and stochastic term \(C\sqrt{\log n/(nh^2)}\), so \(h\asymp a_n\) gives the upper bound \(Ca_n\).  The canonical-square angular-density packing is contained in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\).  Poissonization, the disjoint-cell factorization, the coordinatewise-overlap direct-product lemma, midpoint decoding, and marked subsampling back to exactly \(n\) observations give the matching lower bound \(ca_n\), because the adjacent Poisson compressed laws have relative entropy at most \(2\alpha\log M\) with \(2\alpha<1\).

Suppose instead \(L=4\).  The square has area four and \(f_P\geq1/4\), so
\[
1=\int_{[-1,1]^2}f_P(z)\,dz\geq\int_{[-1,1]^2}\frac14\,dz=1.
\]
Hence \(f_P=1/4\) almost everywhere, and continuity makes the equality pointwise.  At a trimmed boundary point and for all sufficiently small \(s\), each arm-specific circle portion is a half-circle contained in the square, so
\[
Q_{t,P,x}(s)=\frac\pi4s.
\]
Taylor expansion of \(\mu_{t,P}\) through degree \(q-1\), followed by half-circle integration and grouping equal powers of \(s\), gives uniformly bounded coefficients with
\[
\left|\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}-\mu_{t,P}(x)
-\sum_{k=1}^{q-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|\leq Cs^q.
\]
The one-sided radial polynomial Gram matrix is a positive multiple of
\[
\int_0^1uK_\triangle(u)v_q(u)v_q(u)^\top\,du,
\qquad v_q(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^{q-1})^\top,
\]
which is positive definite because a nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on \((0,1)\).  A cutoff local polynomial in signed radius therefore has bias \(Ch^q\), stochastic term \(C\sqrt{\log n/(nh^2)}\), and a negligible cutoff-exception contribution by the same inverse and outcome-moment calculation above.  Balancing gives the distance upper bound \(Cs_{n,q}\).  Conversely, every distance-only rule can be implemented from full score locations, so
\[
R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})
\geq R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})
\geq cs_{n,q}.
\]
This proves the \(L=4\) equivalence.  Finally,
\[
\frac{q}{2q+2}>\frac14\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q>1,
\]
which proves the stated elbow and all boundary cases.
statements.justification: Holding geometry and the causal target fixed reveals the statistical price of releasing only one distance coordinate, and also identifies the no-density-slack exception.
statements.gap: The full-regressor benchmark and location-based boundary theory do not pair their rate with a direct distance-only angular-confounding converse on the identical straight class.
statements.consumer: A data steward can determine whether a distance-only release loses an exponent: it does for \(q>1\) only when \(L>4\), and it does not when \(L=4\).

statements.statement:
There is no density-only weakest regularity threshold for the faster distance frontier.  The operational upper condition is a joint coarea remainder of the density, regression, and boundary geometry.  Precisely, fix an integer \(m\) with \(1\leq m\leq\min\{q,\iota\}\), and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\) be any subclass for which there are constants \(A<\infty\), \(r_*>0\), and \(0<\underline c\leq\overline c<\infty\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal C\), \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<s\leq r_*\),
\[
 \underline c s\leq Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s,
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}-\mu_{t,P}(x)-\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|\leq As^m,
\]
where the coefficient functions are uniformly bounded over \(P,t,x,k\).  Let \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) be the stabilized coordinatewise degree-\((m-1)\) estimator in \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}distance\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\), using the lower radial constant \(\underline c\).  With
\[
 h_n\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(2m+2)},
\]
this estimator belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 \left|\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)\right|
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
If \(m=q\) and \(\mathcal C\) contains, for every sufficiently large \(n\), the uniform-design straight-interface \(q\)-H\"older bump submodel of width \(h_n\) and height proportional to \(h_n^q\) constructed in the proof, then the reverse inequality holds and the displayed rate is exact.  No matching converse is asserted here when \(m<q\).  Independently, every law class containing the shrinking angular-imbalance family generated by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) has distance lower frontier \(ca_n\).  Thus the order-one upper rate is the first-order saturation rate when that hard family is contained, while every \(m\geq2\) yields a faster geometry-sensitive upper rate; the matching contained-bump certificate supplied here applies exactly at \(m=q\).  A condition on \(f_P\) alone is neither necessary nor sufficient to determine the order: the normalized product integrals \(N/Q\), rather than the density in isolation, are the operational objects.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(m\), \(\mathcal C\), and the constants in the statement.  The proof has four parts.

\emph{Population rank and causal centering.}
For \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), write \(S_{P,x}=|D_{P,x}|\).  Coarea and the definition of \(Q_{t,P,x}\) yield, for \(0<h\leq r_*\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)
 =\int_0^1 K_\triangle(u)v_m(u)v_m(u)^\top
 \frac{Q_{t,P,x}(hu)}h\,du.
\]
Consequently, for every \(a\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[
 \underline c\,a^\top G_ma
 \leq a^\top\mathbb E_P\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)a
 \leq \overline c\,a^\top G_ma.
\]
If \(a\neq0\), the polynomial \(a^\top v_m(u)\) cannot vanish on an interval, while \(uK_\triangle(u)>0\) for \(0<u<1\).  Hence \(G_m\) is positive definite and
\[
 \lambda_{\min}\{\mathbb E_P\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}
 \geq\lambda_m(\underline c)>0.
\]
This verifies every rank and inverse condition used below.  The bandwidth restriction makes every invocation of the radial bounds valid, and the lower inequality makes every displayed ratio well defined for \(0<s\leq r_*\).

By \(\mathrm{lem:canonical\text{-}exact\text{-}distance\text{-}regression}\), the conditional mean of \(Y\) at signed radius \((2t-1)s\) is the canonical coarea ratio for almost every positive radius, and its limit at zero is \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\).  Thus the target remains the causal contrast \(\tau_P(x)=\mu_{1,P}(x)-\mu_{0,P}(x)\); the ratio is an identifying regression, not a redefinition of the target.  Write
\[
 g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)
 =\mu_{t,P}(x)+\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k
 +R_{t,P,x}(s),
 \qquad |R_{t,P,x}(s)|\leq As^m.
\]
With
\[
 \beta_{t,P,x}(h)
 =\bigl(\mu_{t,P}(x),hb_{t,1,P}(x),\ldots,
 h^{m-1}b_{t,m-1,P}(x)\bigr)^\top,
\]
the empirical outcome vector decomposes exactly as
\[
 \widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)
 =\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\beta_{t,P,x}(h)
 +B_{t,x}(h)+Z_{t,x}(h),
\]
where \(B_{t,x}(h)\) is obtained by replacing \(Y_i\) with \(R_{t,P,x}(S_{P,x,i})\), and \(Z_{t,x}(h)\) by replacing it with
\(Y_i-g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(S_{P,x,i})\).  This is the polynomial-reproduction identity; it does not assume a population inverse.

The centered radial error has a uniform conditional sub-Gaussian envelope.  Indeed,
\[
 Y-g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(S_{P,x})
 =\{Y-\mu_{t,P}(X)\}
 +\{\mu_{t,P}(X)-g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(S_{P,x})\}.
\]
The first summand satisfies the conditional exponential inequality in \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}subgaussian}\).  Conditional on the signed radius in arm \(t\), the second is centered by the definition of the radial conditional mean and is bounded by \(2L\), because the H\"older ball includes \(\|\mu_{t,P}\|_\infty\leq L\).  For a centered variable \(V\in[-2L,2L]\), convexity of the exponential gives
\[
 \mathbb E(e^{\lambda V})\leq e^{2L^2\lambda^2}.
\]
Conditioning first on \(X\) and then on the signed radius therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 e^{\lambda\{Y-g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(S_{P,x})\}}
 \mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)S_{P,x}
 \right]
 \leq e^{C_L\lambda^2/2}.
\]

\emph{Uniform good-event bound.}
Let \(\varepsilon_n=n^{-3}\).  Since every trimmed boundary is contained in \([-L,L]^2\), it has an \(\varepsilon_n\)-net of cardinality at most \(C_L\varepsilon_n^{-2}\).  For a fixed net point, each Gram summand before division by \(n\) has norm at most \(C_mh^{-2}\), and the upper radial bound implies its second moment is at most \(C_{m,\overline c}h^{-2}\).  Exponential Markov's inequality applied to the bounded-summand log-moment bound
\[
 \log\mathbb E e^{\lambda(W-\mathbb EW)}
 \leq\frac{\lambda^2\mathbb E(W-\mathbb EW)^2}
 {2(1-|\lambda|\|W-\mathbb EW\|_\infty/3)}
\]
gives entrywise concentration.  The preceding conditional sub-Gaussian inequality gives the analogous bound for \(Z_{t,x}(h)\).  A union bound over the fixed number of matrix coordinates, two arms, and the polynomial-size net shows that, for every prescribed \(B>0\), constants in the deviations can be chosen so that an event \(E_n(P)\) satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}P\{E_n(P)^c\}\leq n^{-B}
\]
and, on \(E_n(P)\), uniformly in \(t\) and all net points,
\[
 \left\|\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)
 -\mathbb E_P\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq\frac14\lambda_m(\underline c),
 \qquad
 \left|e_1^\top\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}^{-1}Z_{t,x}(h)\right|
 \leq C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}},
\]
and \(\max_{1\leq i\leq n}|Y_i|\leq C\sqrt{\log n}\).  Here \(nh^2/\log n\to\infty\), which will hold at the selected bandwidth.

On the nonnegative domain, the maps \(u\mapsto K_\triangle(u)v_m(u)\) and \(u\mapsto K_\triangle(u)v_m(u)v_m(u)^\top\), defined by their displayed formulas for \(0\leq u\leq1\) and extended by zero only for \(u>1\), are Lipschitz on \([0,\infty)\).  No extension across \(u=0\) is made or used; this is exactly the relevant domain because \(u=S_{P,x}/h\geq0\).  Also \(|\|X_i-x\|_2-\|X_i-x'\|_2|\leq\|x-x'\|_2\).  Almost surely no sample score lies on the one-dimensional smooth boundary, so the strict arm indicator is unchanged as \(x\) varies along that boundary.  It follows that the Gram oscillation over a mesh cell is at most \(C\varepsilon_nh^{-3}\), and the outcome-vector oscillation is at most
\[
 C\varepsilon_nh^{-3}\left(\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n|Y_i|\right).
\]
At \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2m+2)}\), both terms are smaller than every displayed stochastic order.  Hence the net inequalities extend to all \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), and Weyl's inequality makes the cutoff active everywhere on \(E_n(P)\).

On this event the inverse norm is at most \(2/\lambda_m(\underline c)\).  Since \(|R_{t,P,x}(S)|\leq Ah^m\) on the kernel support, the decomposition and the bounded empirical kernel moment give
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 \left|\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h,\underline c}(x)-\mu_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \leq C\left\{h^m+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}\right\}.
\]
The mesh extension for the target itself uses
\(|\mu_{t,P}(x)-\mu_{t,P}(x')|\leq L\|x-x'\|_2\), which follows from \(q\geq1\).  Taking the difference of the two arms proves the same bound for the causal curve on \(E_n(P)\).

\emph{The concentration complement.}
Failure of \(E_n(P)\) does not imply failure of the eigenvalue cutoff, so both branches must be controlled.  If a cutoff fails, the corresponding intercept is zero and \(|\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq L\).  If it is active, \(\mathrm{lem:stabilized\text{-}distance\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}admissible}\) gives, simultaneously for every \(x\),
\[
 \left|\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h,\underline c}(x)\right|
 \leq C h^{-2}\overline Y_n,
 \qquad \overline Y_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n|Y_i|.
\]
The H\"older envelope and the conditional sub-Gaussian inequality imply \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_PY_i^2\leq C\), and Jensen's inequality therefore gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\overline Y_n^2
 \leq\sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb E_PY_i^2
 \leq C.
\]
Thus Cauchy--Schwarz yields the explicit exceptional contribution
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \mathbf1_{E_n(P)^c}
 \right]
 \leq C\{n^{-B}+h^{-2}n^{-B/2}\}.
\]
Taking, for example, \(B=10\) makes this term negligible at the bandwidth below.  Combining the good and exceptional events gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right]
 \leq C\left\{h^m+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}\right\}
\]
for \(h\leq r_*\) and all sufficiently large \(n\).  Balancing the two displayed terms gives
\[
 h_n\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(2m+2)},
 \qquad
 h_n^m\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
The admissibility lemma makes this one explicit data-driven witness in \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\), so the definition of minimax risk proves the asserted upper bound.

\emph{The valid contained-bump converse.}
Now suppose \(m=q\) and that \(\mathcal C\) contains the stated submodel.  We spell out the witness to verify why the restriction \(m=q\) is necessary.  On the unit square with uniform score density and the horizontal straight interface, choose \(M\asymp h_n^{-1}\) trimmed centers \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) separated by \(3h_n\).  Let \(\phi\in C_c^\infty(B_2(0,1))\) satisfy \(0\leq\phi\leq1\) and \(\phi(0)=1\), and put
\[
 \Delta_n=\eta h_n^q,
 \qquad
 \mu_{0,j}(z)=0,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,j}(z)=\Delta_n\phi((z-x_j)/h_n).
\]
Let \(Y(t)=\mu_{t,j}(X)+\varepsilon_t\), where the \(\varepsilon_t\) are independent standard Gaussian variables, and impose deterministic assignment and consistency.  For every derivative order \(0\leq k\leq q\),
\[
 \|D^k\mu_{1,j}\|_\infty
 \leq C_\phi\eta h_n^{q-k}\leq C_\phi\eta.
\]
After choosing the fixed amplitude \(\eta>0\) small enough, all laws satisfy the common \(q\)-H\"older, variance, sub-Gaussian, support, reach, and two-sided-thickness envelopes.  This derivative calculation is valid because the height is \(h_n^q\).  If instead one used height \(h_n^m\) with \(m<q\), its \(q\)-th derivative would be of order \(h_n^{m-q}\), which diverges; that invalid construction is not used.

Let \(P_0\) denote the same law with both regressions zero.  Conditional normal relative entropy and the fact that a bump occupies score area \(O(h_n^2)\) give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq Cn\Delta_n^2h_n^2
 =C\eta^2nh_n^{2q+2}
 \leq C'\eta^2\log n.
\]
Because \(\log M=(1/(2q+2)+o(1))\log n\), \(\eta\) can be fixed so that the last display is at most \(\alpha\log M\) for some \(\alpha<1/4\).  If \(J\) is uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,M\}\), the log-sum inequality gives
\[
 I(J;O_{1:n})
 \leq\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq\alpha\log M.
\]
For any decoder with error indicator \(E\), conditioning entropy on \(E\) yields
\[
 H(J\mid O_{1:n})\leq\log2+P(E=1)\log M,
\]
and hence \(P(E=1)\geq1-\alpha-o(1)\).  If a boundary-curve estimator had sup-norm error below \(\Delta_n/3\), maximizing its values at the centers would recover \(J\), because the true curve equals \(\Delta_n\) at \(x_J\) and zero at all other centers.  Therefore even the full-location experiment has risk at least \(c\Delta_n\), and the smaller coordinatewise distance decision class does as well.  Since \(\Delta_n\asymp(\log n/n)^{q/(2q+2)}\), this proves the matching lower bound only in the valid case \(m=q\).

For the angular-imbalance clause, use \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\).  In the mean-\(2n\) Poisson experiment its disjoint local point processes are conditionally independent standard-Borel channels and the outside process is bit-independent.  The packing gives adjacent separation \(c_1a_n\) and relative entropy at most \(2\alpha\log M\), where \(2\alpha<1\).  The coordinatewise-overlap direct-product lemma then gives probability at least \(1/2-o(1)\) of at least one bit error even after all cross-center ancillary observations are revealed.  Midpoint thresholding converts sup-norm error below \(c_1a_n/2\) into exact recovery.  Subsampling \(n\) observations whenever the Poisson count of mean \(2n\) exceeds \(n\), whose failure probability is exponentially small by exponential Markov's inequality, returns the fixed-sample lower bound \(ca_n\).

\emph{Why density alone does not determine the order.}
If an arm regression is locally constant on all relevant circles, then \(N_{t,P,x}(s)=\mu_{t,P}(x)Q_{t,P,x}(s)\) exactly, regardless of any differentiability of \(f_P\); density smoothness is therefore not necessary for an arbitrarily high normalized-coarea remainder at that law.  Conversely, fix a straight interface and, near an interior boundary point, use the same bounded positive continuous density in polar coordinates
\[
 f(r,\theta)=c_0\{1+r^\alpha\cos\theta\},
 \qquad 0<\alpha<1,
\]
with a continuous compactly supported localization and a compensating normalization away from the point.  The angular perturbation integrates to zero on every complete circle and tends to zero at the center, so positivity, continuity, normalization, and the radial mass bounds are preserved.  With a constant regression, \(N/Q\) is constant.  With the affine regression \(\mu(z)=z_1\), on an upper half-circle centered at the point,
\[
 \frac{N(s)}{Q(s)}
 =\frac{s\int_0^\pi\cos\theta\{1+s^\alpha\cos\theta\}\,d\theta}
 {\int_0^\pi\{1+s^\alpha\cos\theta\}\,d\theta}
 =\frac12s^{1+\alpha},
\]
which has no order-two polynomial remainder.  Thus the same density can yield different normalized product remainders when paired with different smooth regressions.  The joint ratio \(N/Q\), not \(f_P\) in isolation, is exactly the object controlled in the upper proof.  This completes the proof.

statements.statement:
Let all spaces carrying \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M,S_1,\ldots,S_M\) be standard Borel.  Let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) be independent uniform binary variables.  Conditionally on them, let \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) be independent, with the law of \(Z_j\) depending only on \(\Omega_j\) for \(1\leq j\leq M\), and with the law of \(Z_0\) independent of \((\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M)\).  Suppose decoder \(j\) is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\), where \(S_j\) is a measurable compression of \(Z_j\), and write \(Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b)\) and \(\rho_j=1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Then every such decentralized decoder obeys
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]
In particular, if \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq\kappa\log M\) for all \(j\) and a fixed \(\kappa<1\), then the probability of at least one decoding error is at least \(1/2-o(1)\).
statements.proof_tex:
For each \(j\), dominate \(Q_{j,0}\) and \(Q_{j,1}\) by their sum and write their densities as \(q_{j,0}\) and \(q_{j,1}\).  The common subprobability measure has density \(q_{j,0}\wedge q_{j,1}\) and mass
\[
 \rho_j=\int(q_{j,0}\wedge q_{j,1})
 =1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
Generate the binary compressed experiment by first drawing an ambiguity indicator \(A_j\), independent of \(\Omega_j\), with \(\Pr(A_j=1)=\rho_j\).  On \(A_j=1\), draw \(S_j\) from the normalized common submeasure, independently of \(\Omega_j\); on \(A_j=0\), draw it from the normalized residual measure corresponding to \(\Omega_j\).  Zero-mass cases may be assigned arbitrary kernels because their indicators then have probability zero.  Use independent indicators and seeds across \(j\).  Because all observation spaces are standard Borel, a regular conditional kernel for \(Z_j\) given \((S_j,\Omega_j)\) exists; applying it reconstructs the original local experiment.  Independently draw the bit-independent ancillary \(Z_0\) from its fixed law.  The conditional product premise shows that this coupling preserves the joint law of the stated experiment.

Fix the ambiguity indicators, all non-bit seeds, and the bits outside the ambiguous coordinate set \(A=\{j:A_j=1\}\).  If \(A\neq\varnothing\), consider the configurations of \((\Omega_j:j\in A)\) on which every decoder is correct.  Two configurations that differ only at coordinate \(j\in A\) cannot both succeed: decoder \(j\) sees the same \(S_j\), the same \(Z_{-j}\), and the same \(Z_0\) at the two endpoints, so its output is unchanged while the correct bit is reversed.  The successful configurations therefore form an independent set in the \(|A|\)-dimensional hypercube.  Pairing vertices along any coordinate shows that this set has at most \(2^{|A|-1}\) elements.  The ambiguous bits remain uniform, so conditional exact-success probability is at most \(1/2\).  If \(A=\varnothing\), it is at most one.  Averaging proves
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq\Pr(A=\varnothing)+\frac12\Pr(A\neq\varnothing)
 =\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]

For the relative-entropy consequence, define the Hellinger affinity \(H_j=\int\sqrt{q_{j,0}q_{j,1}}\).  Jensen's inequality under \(Q_{j,0}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\geq-2\log H_j.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\sqrt{1-H_j^2}
 \leq\sqrt{1-e^{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})}}.
\]
Since \(1-\sqrt{1-u}\geq u/2\) for \(0\leq u\leq1\),
\[
 \rho_j\geq\frac12e^{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})}
 \geq\frac12M^{-\kappa}.
\]
Therefore \(\prod_j(1-\rho_j)\leq\exp\{-M^{1-\kappa}/2\}=o(1)\), and the preceding exact-success bound implies an any-error probability at least \(1/2-o(1)\).

statements.statement:
For every integer \(m\geq1\), cutoff constant \(c>0\), bandwidth \(h>0\), law \(P\), and boundary point \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), the rule in \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}distance\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\) is a measurable function of \(U_{n,P}(x)\), and therefore its arm difference is an element of \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\).  Moreover, on the active-cutoff branch,
\[
 \left|\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h,c}(x)\right|
 \leq
 \frac{2\sqrt m}{c\lambda_{\min}(G_m)}h^{-2}
 \left(\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n|Y_i|\right),
\]
whereas on the failed-cutoff branch the arm intercept is exactly zero.
statements.proof_tex:
All coordinates in the construction are Borel functions of the pairs \((Y_i,D_{P,x,i})\): absolute value and the strict sign indicators are Borel, \(K_\triangle\) and \(v_m\) are continuous, finite sums and products are Borel, the minimum eigenvalue is continuous on the symmetric matrices, and matrix inversion is continuous on the invertible matrices.  The active branch is contained in the set on which the minimum eigenvalue is at least \(c\lambda_{\min}(G_m)/2>0\); the other branch is assigned the fixed value zero.  Thus the piecewise formula is Borel.  It uses only \(U_{n,P}(x)\), including the declared convention when \(D_{P,x,i}=0\), so the definition of \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) gives admissibility.

On the active branch, the spectral cutoff gives
\[
 \left\|\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}^{-1}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq\frac{2}{c\lambda_{\min}(G_m)}.
\]
Because \(0\leq K_\triangle\leq1\) and \(\|v_m(u)\|_2\leq\sqrt m\) on \(0\leq u\leq1\),
\[
 \left\|\widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\right\|_2
 \leq\frac{\sqrt m}{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n|Y_i|.
\]
Multiplication by \(e_1^\top\), whose Euclidean norm is one, proves the displayed bound.  The failed-cutoff assertion is exactly the zero convention in the construction.

sampling_model.design: A boundary discontinuity design with a known binary assignment partition of a compact bivariate score support.
sampling_model.overlap: Each arm has probability mass at least \(c_{-}r^2\) in every boundary ball of radius \(r\) for \(0<r\leq r_0\); \(f_P\leq L\) yields the derived upper estimate \(\pi Lr^2\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The score density is bounded and continuous but has no class-uniform derivative or continuity modulus. Exact-distance regressions use the canonical coarea ratio on positive-denominator radii and the H\"older regression representative on zero-denominator radii. Both distance upper bounds use the fixed triangular kernel and degree zero; the comparison experiment permits estimators to use full score locations jointly.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The identification theorem supplies the distance-based causal functional; the smooth-bias theorem is fixed-law; the published nonparametric converse has order \(n^{-1/4}\), and its discussion predicts a missing uniform logarithm.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The rectifiable frontier establishes the logarithmic order on a separate two-sided-thickness class, the smooth theorem proves first-order saturation without a common density modulus, and the coarea theorem proves the order-\(m\) upper rate with a matching contained-bump converse only at \(m=q\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The location-based method retains the bivariate score and motivates the full-location comparison experiment.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The straight-class theorem proves the full-location benchmark and compares it with distance-only rates separately for \(L>4\) and \(L=4\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Stone's global H\"older benchmark in dimension two has order \((\log n/n)^{q/(2q+2)}\).
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The straight-class full-location theorem derives this order and shows that the distance order coincides with it at \(L=4\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Separated alternatives and multiple testing motivate logarithmic sup-norm converses under information restrictions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present converse adds an explicit overlap-coupling direct-product certificate for coordinatewise distance decisions with cross-center ancillary data.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Positive reach and smooth embedded-manifold geometry provide geometric background.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The smooth saturation proof verifies the unit-square straight chart directly and shows that geometry alone does not determine the coordinatewise distance rate.

tldr: The coordinatewise distance experiment has a sharp first-order uniform frontier even when the assignment boundary and outcome regressions are arbitrarily smooth. On the primitive rectifiable class with an inspectable arm-specific two-sided design-thickness condition, \(R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}})\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/4}\). The same rate holds on the endpoint-trimmed smooth class because bounded continuous score densities have no common angular regularity modulus; a straight-boundary angular-density packing with affine regressions supplies the converse. On the identical straight geometry, full score locations recover \((\log n/n)^{q/(2q+2)}\), strictly faster for \(q>1\). A central open question asks which primitive density or angular-balance regularity produces a transition to a faster distance-only frontier.

project_justification.gap: Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 6, gives an \(n^{-1/4}\) pointwise-style lower bound over its stated nonparametric class, while the following discussion predicts that uniform estimation carries a logarithmic factor. Their Theorem 3(ii) is a fixed-law interior smooth-bias result and does not determine a class-uniform minimax rate when continuous score densities have no common modulus.
project_justification.niche: The coordinatewise distance release discards angular locations. A primitive two-sided design-thickness condition stabilizes local estimation and supplies separated boundary neighborhoods, while unrestricted shrinking-scale angular imbalance can keep the induced radial regression only first-order regular even on a straight boundary.
project_justification.fill: The rectifiable theorem establishes the predicted logarithmic phenomenon on its own transparent primitive class. The smooth saturation theorem shows that geometry alone does not improve that frontier, and the straight-class comparison isolates the lost information by proving the faster Stone exponent for the full-location experiment.

related_work: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance is the anchor. Its Theorem 1 supplies distance-based BATEC identification as background; the present supporting coarea lemma fixes a canonical exact-distance conditional representative, including its values on zero-denominator radii, for the proposal's primitive classes. Its Theorem 6 proves an \(n^{-1/4}\) lower bound over a class defined by independent sampling, bounded continuous density on compact support, a rectifiable support boundary, H\"older regression, and bounded continuous variance; Assumption 2(iv)'s Gram condition is not a premise of that theorem. The discussion after Theorem 6 conjectures that the missing logarithm reflects the pointwise lower-bound construction. The rectifiable result here establishes that logarithmic phenomenon on a separately defined primitive two-sided-thickness class, with no asserted inclusion or transfer. Theorem 3(ii) of the same paper is a fixed-law interior two-intersection bias statement; its supplemental angular-integral differentiation does not supply a common higher-order bias constant over the present bounded continuous density envelope, and the saturation theorem does not challenge the published fixed-law result. CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Location supplies the full-location benchmark experiment, while CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Survey documents the applied prevalence of location- and distance-based boundary analyses. Stone1982OptimalGlobal supplies the classical bivariate sup-norm exponent recovered by the full-location risk on the straight subclass. ChenChristensen2018SupNorm informs the separated-alternative multiple-testing architecture but studies a different inverse-regression experiment. AamariAaronLevrard2021Boundary supplies background for positive reach and \(C^2\) embedded-manifold geometry and is the source for the positive-reach premise. It is not the source of the proposal's two-sided length envelope, injective \(C^{\iota+2}\) chart, uniform chart-derivative envelope, lower chart-speed bound, or arm-specific design-thickness condition.
technical_internal_limitation: The decision restriction is coordinatewise: \(\widehat{\tau}_n(x)\) may use \(U_{n,P}(x)\) but may not triangulate score locations from distances released at other boundary points. A joint multi-center release is a different experiment. Exact-radius conditionals are only determined almost everywhere: the canonical representative uses the coarea ratio where \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\) and the existing H\"older representative \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\) otherwise. Two-sided thickness ensures only that positive-denominator radii accumulate at zero; it does not imply positivity at every radius. The angular-density packing must explicitly construct bounded continuous density perturbations whose imbalance varies at scale \(a_n\), verify common density, tail, variance, H\"older, assignment-partition, reach, and arm-mass constants, keep the straight geometry and affine regressions, and prove the stated compressed-law Kullback--Leibler and packing bounds. Rough density by itself is not a lower-bound proof. For fixed \(P\), the higher-order angular integrals in Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 3(ii), may be differentiable; the diagnostic point is only that no uniform derivative bound follows from this proposal's density envelope. The primitive class here and the anchor's nonparametric class are distinct, and no inclusion is asserted.
honest_scope: The theorem-level targets are rate equivalences, not exact asymptotic constants. Exact-distance conditional expectations are identified only up to null radial sets; the canonical coarea representative fills those radii with \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\), and H\"older continuity makes its boundary limit unique without assuming a positive circle denominator at every radius. The rectifiable result establishes the predicted logarithmic phenomenon only under the novel primitive two-sided design-thickness condition; the logarithmic frontier on the exact nonparametric class of Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 6, remains open. The smooth theorem concerns the fixed endpoint-trimmed target and uses no density modulus beyond continuity and fixed upper and lower bounds. Its lower bound has an explicit compressed-experiment construction obligation on a straight two-half-plane submodel with affine regressions. The full-location Stone exponent is stated only for the separately defined full-location decision class and is strictly faster than the distance exponent only when \(q>1\). The weakest empirically meaningful regularity producing a faster distance-only frontier is open.
